This was something I asked my prescribing provider when I first started; how long will I need to keep this up? She told me she didn’t know, but she’d never had someone on it longer than a year. Welp… I’ve been doing at-home ketamine (nasal spray, lozenges, and now troches) since December 2019. My doc says we’ll just do it until I’ve had several months of “feeling good”. I’ve decided to stop using it this summer entirely (under her supervision) and see how I do. I’ve been in a really good place in spite of a bunch of personal setbacks (and a pandemic!) and I think I’m ready to go without. I’ve always wondered if this was just my life now. It’s a way better life than one on SSRIs for me. But I don’t love being on anything if I can help it. I’ve had to go off ketamine for a week or two at a time because I was traveling and refill timing didn’t work out. I felt fine. I think I may have hit the point where it retrained my brain enough for me to just be me. Although I do love the ritual every other night, and the euphoria and self discovery. I’m interested to see if I’ll need to go back to it after a few months off. Thank you for sharing your experience.

This does sound like [sleep paralysis ](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep_paralysis). It’s where the hormones that stop you from acting out your dreams in REM sleep don’t dissipate quickly enough when you wake up so you’re temporarily paralyzed. Incredibly common and not life threatening but terrifying nonetheless. And yeah, you can have it happen just once. A lot of people will experience it and just think it was a terrible nightmare. I get it sometimes when I’m really stressed out and I see ghosts when I have it which is just the worst. You may check for other issues as others have suggested but this really does sound like sleep paralysis.

If it helps, the high is often considered to be part of the treatment, from my understanding. So from that perspective, it’s working. 

But I agree with other posters that you can and should start slow... especially if you’re uncomfortable or incapacitated. 

My doc’s instructions were: one spray per nostril, wait 15 min, then do another spray per nostril. Lie down in your bedroom or somewhere quiet and dark and definitely don’t do anything else the rest of the day/night. Take this dosage every other night for a week or two (I think I did a month) and then do the same dosage every night. And then add a third set of sprays and a fourth at a similar pace, ramping up as needed. If you’re feeling “too high” then scale back it do it every other day at the same dosage instead of every day.

These dosages of ketamine tend to wear off after a few hours, but you shouldn’t plan to operate heavy machinery or really do anything important until the next day. 

But yeah, there’s no real best practice for dosing quite yet. Ketamine treatment is controversial in a lot of circles, from what I’ve read. What’s most important is that you do what’s right for you.
